challengeTypes: identify: What type of angle is shown? (a 45 degree angle — Acute vs Right vs Obtuse vs Straight)
sort: Drag each angle to its correct classification (45 degrees = Acute | 90 degrees = Right | 120 degrees = Obtuse | 30 degrees = Acute | 180 degrees = Straight | 60 degrees = Acute)
identify: How many lines of symmetry does a square have? (4 vs 2 vs 1 vs 0)
sort: Drag each shape to its correct number of lines of symmetry (Square = 4 | Rectangle = 2 | Equilateral Triangle = 3 | Circle = Infinite | Scalene Triangle = 0 | Isosceles Triangle = 1)
identify: Which 3D shape has rotational symmetry around its vertical axis? (Cylinder vs Cube vs Cuboid vs all of them)
sort: Drag each 3D shape to its correct net (Cube = cross of 6 squares | Cylinder = rectangle + 2 circles | Cone = sector + circle | Cuboid = cross of 6 rectangles)
identify: A cube has how many faces, edges, and vertices? (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices vs 6 faces, 8 edges, 12 vertices vs 12 faces, 6 edges, 8 vertices vs 8 faces, 12 edges, 6 vertices)

sort: Drag each object to its symmetry type (Human body = Reflection symmetry | Wheel = Rotational symmetry | Cube = Both reflection and rotational | Irregular rock = No symmetry | Cylinder = Rotational symmetry | Rectangle = Reflection symmetry)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Angles and measures — an angle is formed when two rays meet at a point (vertex). Measured in degrees with a protractor. (2) Classification — Right angle = exactly 90 degrees (square corner). Acute angle = less than 90 degrees. Obtuse angle = more than 90 but less than 180 degrees. Straight angle = exactly 180 degrees. (3) Identification — look at the opening between the rays. Use a protractor: place center on vertex, base on one ray, read the degree on the other ray. (4) Symmetry in 3D shapes — a cube has symmetry planes cutting through opposite faces and through opposite edges. Human body has bilateral (reflection) symmetry. Buildings often have reflection symmetry. (5) Reflection symmetry in 2D — a line that divides a shape into two identical mirror halves. Square has 4 lines. Rectangle has 2. Equilateral triangle has 3. Circle has infinite lines. Rotational symmetry — when a shape looks the same after rotation. Square has rotational symmetry of order 4 (90, 180, 270, 360 degrees). Equilateral triangle has order 3. (6) Nets — a net is a flat 2D shape that folds into a 3D shape. Cube net = 6 squares in a cross pattern. Cylinder net = 1 rectangle + 2 circles. Cone net = 1 sector (part of circle) + 1 circle (base). Cuboid net = 6 rectangles in a cross pattern. Misconceptions: 'a right angle is the largest angle' (WRONG — obtuse and straight angles are larger than 90 degrees), 'a square has only 2 lines of symmetry' (WRONG — it has 4: 2 through midpoints of opposite sides and 2 through opposite vertices/diagonals), 'a cube net is always a cross' (WRONG — there are 11 different valid cube nets, the cross is just one common one), 'rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry are the same' (WRONG — reflection is mirror image across a line, rotational is turning around a point), 'all 3D shapes have symmetry' (WRONG — irregular shapes like a rock have no symmetry).
